enAudit: NEW — G1-270: the instruction "Double the group, then halve it. Small numbers to start." describes a two-step operation on one group, but the render is four INDEPENDENT cards, each carrying its own label (double / half) and its own different set of foxes (3+3, half of 6, 2+2, half of 2). The child never halves a group they doubled. This is a flow the page does not have; the honest sentence is "read the label on each card: double or half".

NEW — K-299: the title "Copy the Picture Using Letters and Numbers" names a property it SHARES with K-300, which is also labelled (A-H / 1-8). Same defect class as the already-fixed G1-263. Against K-298 the true delta is the labels; against K-300 it is the smaller 6x6 grid, and only one of those is in the title.

NEW — G1-258 / G1-259: the same shared-property class again. "With a Word Bank" and "Choose from the Word Bank" both name the bank, which BOTH pages have (bank:true). The real delta is starter:true — G1-258 prints the first letter of every word and G1-259 does not. The instructions do carry it; the titles do not, so the two pages are indistinguishable in a SERP.

NEW — G2-294: every card on this page is a canBuy, and in two independently seeded renders ALL THREE answers were "no" (45 vs 35+15=50, 40 vs 35+30=65, 50 vs 40+35=75). A three-card yes/no page whose answers are identical can be completed correctly by writing one word three times, with no arithmetic. The generator needs a mixed-verdict constraint, the way the sum-ceiling checks constrain the number ranges.

NEW — G2-285: the instruction never mentions that some word chips carry a supporting picture (pics:true — dolphin, seagull, giraffe are illustrated). That picture support is the ONLY thing separating this face from G2-286, whose instruction DOES say "No pictures to help". The contrast is stated on one side of the pair only, so G2-285 reads as the generic face of the family.

NEW — G1-268: "A bottom brick is missing. Use the brick above to find it." describes only the one missing bottom brick, but every other brick in all four walls is also empty and has to be built. The instruction under-describes the task a child actually faces; "then build the rest of the wall" is missing.

NEW — G1-256: the number of the day is drawn from 11-19, so "ten more" is always 21-29 — OUTSIDE the 0-20 number line printed on the same page (line.max = 20). Not wrong, but the page supplies a number line that cannot be used to check the very answer the page asks for. Either the line should run to 30 or the ten-more box belongs on the up-to-99 face.

NEW — G2-300: the title "Your Own Words" and the instruction "No sentence starters" overclaim. A word bank of six labelled nouns is still printed on the page (nouns:6). The real delta against G2-299 is the absence of the sentence starters (starters:null), not the absence of supplied vocabulary. "No sentence starters this time" alone would be honest; "your own words" is not.

NEW — G2-293: beyond the duplicated card already reported, EVERY card on the page is paid with the same two 25c coins, so the tendered amount is 50 on all three. "Count the coins paid" is therefore never a real sub-task — the child counts the identical pair three times. Also card 1 asks "How much money does Mia get back?" while cards 2 and 3 ask "How much change does X get?" — two registers for one question type on one page.

KNOWN (seen, corroborating) — G1-264: "Two words start alike" over a page of SIX words in TWO pairs (baby/boat and scooter/swing). Both pairs need the second letter; the singular framing describes one.

KNOWN (seen, corroborating) — G2-281: the same names-need-capitals gap that was fixed in G2-282. Two of the four sentences begin with a lowercase proper name ("anna has a big fox", "ben likes the little donkey"), but needCaps is 0, the legend carries only "Capital letter" and "End mark", and the instruction says only "a capital letter and a full stop". A child who capitalises just the first word has not finished the sentence.

KNOWN (seen, corroborating) — the G3 grouping stories state the arrangement as already done while the strip is drawn ungrouped, in rows of ten: G3-373 ("Ben makes groups of 5" over a flat strip), G3-374 card 2 ("arranges 10 cranberries in rows of 5" drawn as one row of 10), G3-375 card 2 ("20 koalas in rows of 5" drawn as 2 rows of 10) and G3-376 card 3. The rows-of-ten layout is deliberate (it must not restate the quotient), so the fix belongs in the story wording, not the picture.

DATA (fixed by the regeneration, recorded) — the first out/b2var-faces.json I read carried three stale themes (G1-283, G3-372, G3-376 all said vehicles) and a sweep path g1283-vehicles.png that did not exist on disk, while loadType(id).i18n.en already held the corrected English. The generator, not the exported table, is the source of truth; a panel briefed only from the table would have named three themes wrongly.

KNOWN (third independent confirmation, with the Italian render) — G2-306 "Find both capitals, not just the first" was false on the page it built. ends:["."] drops every question frame, and all nine surviving {name} frames in the it bank open WITH the name ("{name} vede tre {noun}.", "{name} conta cinque {noun}.", "{name} ha sei {noun}." …), so the name IS the sentence-initial capital. Rendered it/animals: "giulia ha sei ippopotami" / "giulia disegna quattro gufi" / "aurora conta cinque elefanti" — three lines, three single capitals, zero second capitals. Face since cut in ac61e117; recorded because the render is the concrete artefact behind the cross-locale measurement.

NEW (still live, survives the cut) — G2-274 draws its lane names with rng.sample(bank.names, 2) PER LANE and never excludes names already used on the page. The cut G2-306 render showed giulia on two of three lines; the same code paints the SHIPPED G2-274 / G2-281 / G2-282, where a repeated name is merely dull rather than fatal. The it bank holds eight names against a 3-5 lane page, so a per-page distinct-name constraint is cheap and belongs beside the existing needCaps guard.

KNOWN (third independent confirmation) — the five base-identical faces. K-312, G1-284, G1-290, G2-309 and G3-377 each spread base.difficulty[2] with an EMPTY override while the waves publish difficulties:[2], so each rendered the already-live K-284 / G1-245 / G1-244 / G2-278 / G3-370 with a new theme and a new title. Reached independently here while writing the Italian copy, before ac61e117 landed: K-284 "Ricalca e scrivi le parole" already IS the ≤9-letter page and G1-245 "Ordine alfabetico" already IS six words, so a title naming length or card-count promises a distinction the base already owns — the K-299 / G1-258-259 shared-property defect one level up.

NEW — K-308 / G1-285 / G2-304 (all three still live) inherit d1 (window:10, count:20), so only TEN dots are numbered and the rest of the outline is already printed. Confirmed on the K-308 render: labels 10→1, coral start ring on the 10, grey pre-printed remainder closing the figure. None of the three English instructions says so, while their d1 sibling K-294 does ("to finish the picture") — a child who counts 10, 9, 8 … 1 and stops has not finished the drawing. G1-294 (window:null) is the one face of the four where the numbers run the whole way, and the only one whose English gets it right. The Italian for all four now states it or its absence.

NEW — K-311 (still live): the English is right about the mechanics and wrong about the family. With traceLane:false there is no dashed lane anywhere — render: gabbiano / pesce / elefante / delfino printed SOLID on the card with two empty rails each — so the family verb "Trace" does not apply to this face at all. Brief rule 5 (inherit the genre head) and rule 4 (honesty) collide here; Italian renamed it (Ricopia la parola dal modello) rather than inherit Ricalca. Flagged so the other ten panels are not marked down for the same call.

NEW — G1-286 (still live) is the one doubles-halves face whose HALF cards run to 2×10=20 pictures in two rows. The English "Count the bigger groups, double them, and halve them" repeats the G1-270 defect the last panel filed: the child never doubles and then halves the same group — each card carries its own label and its own set. Render confirms four independent cards (il doppio 7+7 · la metà 18 · il doppio 6+6 · la metà). The Italian says only "count the bigger groups", which is what the page actually asks.

BUILD (pre-dates the cut; still worth recording) — wsg-wb2varit-g2309-vehicles-d2-it failed the QA overflow lint (four divs and an svg past the page box) on every attempt: with an 87-char instruction, with a 43-char one, and with a 6-char title plus a 9-char instruction, so it was NOT the header copy. The same face built clean on it+animals, it+toys, it+fruits and on de/es/nl/fi + vehicles, and the base G2-278 vehicles/d2/it had shipped — i.e. picture-writing d2 on Italian vehicles is seed-fragile, and the surviving G2-299 / G2-300 / G2-278 sit on the same stack.

DATA — out/b2var-faces.json still holds only the first 64 faces: no wave-2 id is in it and out/b2var-sweep/ has no renders for them, so a panel following the brief literally ("the exact path is in the sweep field") has nothing to look at. I built the wave instead (cli.js generate --wave waves/wave-b2var-it.json --types=…) and read the thumbnails out of the staged ZIPs; that should be the brief's wave-2 instruction. Related: waves/wave-b2var-*.json still list the six cut ids and THEME still pins five of them.

MEASURED — the Italian description budget is about half the Spanish figure the brief quotes, and the brief should carry the number. The it lead is "Scheda stampabile gratis: <TITLE> Scheda di esercizi (<Tema>) per <Livello>." plus " Scarica il PDF gratis.", costing 84-103 chars BEFORE the title, so the JOINT budget is titleLen + instructionLen ≤ 84 themeless and ≤ 65-69 themed. All seven surviving instructions are 25-47 chars. On most it faces the core already exceeds 120 with no middle at all, so the 120 floor never binds and only the 170 ceiling does — the exception is the write-the-word family, whose it skill sentence DOES band and must also be beaten: G1-291 needed its title cut from 33 to 26 chars to open a window at all.

NEW (wave 2, build-breaking) — G1-298 and G1-299 are listed in gen-b2var-waves.js THEMELESS, but doubles-halves carries themeAxis {applicable:true} and G1-247.build() calls safeNouns(theme) unconditionally, so theme:null throws 'resolve: theme not in cache manifest: null' (measured; both build clean on fruits). They are therefore NOT themeless: they fall through to the positional round-robin in enumerate.js, which is precisely the class the file's own docblock says pinning eliminated after G1-247 shipped on toys in 11 locales. Their manifest.theme, deck slug and landing URL will carry a theme nobody chose, and it shifts if a type is inserted before them. Pin both in THEME and remove them from THEMELESS.

NEW — K-309: the English 'Join the dots in alphabet order, from a to t' hard-codes a 26-letter strip. The sequence is read from COLLATION[loc].strip, and Italian prints 21 letters (no j k w x y), so the 20 dots run a -> v. Measured on the it render: the labels end at v and the counting strip below prints a b c d e f g h i l m n o p q r s t u v. Every non-EN locale ends on a different letter; only the EN sentence names one, and it is the wrong one for at least it (and for any locale whose strip is not a-z).

NEW — G1-292 is d3 (level3:true), so ARTICLES.it.chipsD3 applies and the page renders FOUR bins: il / lo / la / l'. Any brief or copy that says 'il/la' describes d1. Worse, the bins are not guaranteed to be reachable: itKey() sends a word to 'lo' only for a masculine noun starting s+consonant / z / gn / ps / pn / x / y / i+vowel, and in two independently seeded toys/it draws the 'lo' bin had ZERO correct words (one draw also left l' empty). A four-column sort can therefore print a column with no correct answer. K-306/K-307 already carry a gender-mix guard; this face needs the same coverage constraint over its chip set.

NEW — G2-311: 'Two sentences ran together, and one of them is a question' asserts of EVERY card what needQ:1 guarantees of exactly ONE of the three lanes. Measured on the it render: lane 1 carried the question ('... chi disegna quattro lamponi per aurora'), lanes 2 and 3 were two statements each. A child told there is a question on every line will invent one. The Italian says only 'separate the sentences and choose the end mark'.

NEW — G1-302 (showCap:false) prints proper names in lowercase: the it render shows 'leonardo' and 'aurora' as word tiles. In the capitals-punctuation family that is correct by design (the checklist chip literally reads 'Nomi propri' and restoring them is the task). In sentence-building it is not: the task is word ORDER, the page never asks for capitalisation, and the child copies each tile onto the ruling exactly as printed. A lowercase proper name is an orthographic error in all 11 locales. Either exclude the {name} frames when showCap is false, or keep the name's capital and accept that it only half-leaks the start (a name can sit mid-sentence).

NEW — G2-313: the slug is number-walls-to-100 while baseMin 5 / baseMax 12 over four courses puts the apex between 40 and 8*12 = 96, so 100 is unreachable. Measured apexes on the it render: 60, 70, 46, 49. The English TITLE is right ('two-digit answers'); the slug is the part that reaches the landing URL and it promises a range the generator cannot produce.

NEW (asset) — toys/scooter: the artwork is a motor scooter (a Vespa) while the it vocab word is 'monopattino', a kick scooter. It is picture-only on G1-286 but is printed as a WORD CHIP on G1-292, where the child reads 'monopattino' beside nothing that resembles one. Same class as the vocab arc's root cause: the word was checked, the picture was not.

NEW (asset) — toys/girl: the artwork is a doll and the vocab key is 'girl', so K-315 prints 'RAGAZZA' under a doll (EN would print 'GIRL'). In a toys theme a child names it 'bambola'. The mismatch is in the asset/key pairing, so it hits all 11 locales, not just it.

NEW (layout, cosmetic) — G1-291 spreads d1, whose row height was sized for a word bank, with bank:false; K-315 spreads d3 with traceLane:false. Both leave roughly half of every card blank on the render. Nothing is wrong on the page, it simply prints thin, and a card-height override would recover the space.

NEW (shared template, affects all 100 it faces) — the it description lead reads 'Scheda stampabile gratis: <TITLE> Scheda di esercizi (<Tema>) per <Livello>.' There is no separator between the title and the second 'Scheda', so the two run together in the SERP, and the noun 'Scheda' appears twice inside eleven words. Not a per-face copy issue and not fixable from this draft; recorded because it is the first thing an Italian teacher reads.

NEW — G1-293: pics:true illustrates the NOUN chips only (domino, bicicletta, pastelli, scivolo, dinosauro carry a picture; cantare, dormire, mangiare, correre, bere do not), so the noun/verb sort can be completed without reading a single word.
